scope: The black Sculpted display cover with bowed sides, snapped onto the plain-grooved Sculpted tip printed beside it.
tried: the printed cover snapped onto the printed tip
observations: On the prints that just finished, the fit turned out wonderful. Best faucet display cover fit so far, and very tight/firm. It is good enough. You can see in the photos it is not perfect though. When viewed from below both the aft and fore side are improved from the previous prints. On the fore side specifically we can see that at least from this angle, the very foremost tip of the wing there is *not* contacting the surface, so the bend was a total success there it seems, with that very tip on the very bottom as we look at it from below. And on the aft side it is almost like that, but still a bit of a ramp where you can see the tip kissing the surface. But on the fore side, as we bring the camera around the side you see we do make quite a lot of contact with the surface there for a bit, and then we get gaps again.
So, I'm thinking some further small adjustments could go a long ways.

agent_reading.author: Claude, from the photos; not Derek's words.
agent_reading.sides: Between the lips' ends each side sits evenly. Past each lip's end the side stands off the tube, most beside the lip and less toward the tip. The fore tip stays off the tube. The aft tip touches it.
agent_reading.front: From the fore corner the cover's front edge lies on the tip up the lower part of its run, then stands open over the cap, widest at the top of the arch.
agent_reading.tip_end: The band by the dispense face still shows ripples on this plate, which printed with part cooling there. Derek has not said how it compares.
agent_reading.limits: Photographs only. No opening was measured.
